data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes only when the subject is installed under a prior failure ritual; the 3/26 is the expected residue of a one-repository, one-author, one-week confound where the same care produced both the test and the mutation generator, so the test's constraining power is circular by construction.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the mutation set is shown to be generated by a model that had not read the acceptance record, the circularity claim weakens.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a second repository with different authorship shows the same 3/26 distribution, the one-author confound is not explanatory.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 compile.py loss is in a code region the author explicitly tested, the escape is not outside the author's model.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4 to 6/7 guarded-module results are replicated under independent mutation generation, the care-circularity is insufficient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mutations were proposed by models that had read the acceptance record, so the mutation distribution is not independent of the test's own history. A test that constrains its subject should show a sharp drop in surviving mutations exactly where the pre-installed failure was planted; but because the same author wrote the test, the registry, and the mutation prompts in the same week, any such drop is indistinguishable from the author's own care reproducing itself. The 1/9 compile.py loss is the one mutation that escaped this circularity \u2014 a mutation outside the author's own mental model of what the test should catch \u2014 and its escape is the only non-tautological signal in the record.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
